title: AgentLeak: Cloning Stronger LLM Agent Capabilities onto Weaker Agents Beyond Skill Stealing
abstract: arXiv:2609.07131v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly achieve long-horizon tasks by combining foundation models with explicit skills and implicit procedural knowledge acquired through execution. The resulting task-solving capabilities have become valuable proprietary assets, raising a new security question: can a substantially weaker attacker-controlled agent acquire the capabilities of a stronger proprietary agent through limited black-box interaction? Existing skill-stealing attacks recover explicit skill artifacts, yet we show that artifact leakage does not necessarily transfer capability: a weaker agent may possess the same skills but still fail because it lacks procedural behaviors implicitly realized by the stronger agent. Our key insight is that the skill execution gap itself forms a leakage surface, where missing behaviors are exposed through observable differences between successful victim executions and failed attacker executions. B

translated_title: AgentLeak：将更强的LLM智能体能力克隆到更弱的智能体上——超越技能窃取
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）智能体日益通过将基础模型与通过执行获得的显式技能和隐式程序性知识相结合来完成长周期任务。由此产生的任务解决能力已成为有价值的专有资产，这引发了一个新的安全问题：一个明显更弱的、受攻击者控制的智能体能否通过有限的黑盒交互获取更强专有智能体的能力？现有的技能窃取攻击能够恢复显式的技能工件，但我们表明，工件泄露并不必然意味着能力转移：较弱的智能体可能拥有相同的技能，却仍然失败，因为它缺乏由更强智能体所隐式实现的程序性行为。我们的关键洞察是，技能执行差距本身构成一个泄露面，缺失的行为会通过成功的受害者执行与失败的攻击者执行之间的可观察差异暴露出来。
tldr: 该论文揭示技能执行差距本身构成一个新的泄露面，攻击者可通过对比黑盒交互中成功与失败执行之间的可观察差异，将更强LLM智能体的隐式程序性行为克隆到更弱的智能体上，实现超越传统技能窃取的能力窃取。
en_tdlr: The paper reveals that the skill execution gap itself forms a new leakage surface, enabling a weaker agent to clone the implicit procedural behaviors of a stronger proprietary agent through black-box interaction by exploiting observable differences between successful and failed executions, going beyond traditional skill stealing.
